statement.p: Let a, h, and k be arbitrary real numbers with a\neq 0, and let f be the function given by the rule f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k.
Which of the following statements are true about f? Select all that apply.

li.p: The graph of y=f(x) is a line.
The maximum value of f(x) is h.
An extreme value occurs at the point (h,k).
If a>0, then f has a global minimum.
If a>0, then f has a global maximum.
The graph of y=f(x) is a parabola.

statement.p: Next we use some calculus to develop familiar ideas from a different perspective. To start, treat a, h, and k as constants and compute f'(x).
Find a critical value of f. (This will depend on at least one of a, h, and k.)
Assume that a\lt 0. Make a derivative sign chart for f. Based on this information, classify the critical value of f as a maximum or minimum."

solution.p: The graph of f is a parabola that will open up if a>0, in which case it has a global minimum at (h,k). The derivative is f'(x)=2a(x-h), so there is a critical value at x=h. It is easy to use a derivative sign chart to confirm that this critical value yields a maximum if a\lt 0.
